newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Jewish group blames Argentine security "Nazis". [CORRECTED 01:22 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Jewish group blames Argentine security "Nazis". [CORRECTED 01:22 GMT]

text.p: A leading Argentine Jewish group on Tuesday accused "Nazis in the state's repressive apparatus" of a spate of anti-Semitic attacks, calling the local Jewish community "the most vulnerable in the world."

"The attack on La Tablada Jewish cemetery confirms Nazis continue acting in Argentina with total impunity," the conservative Jewish congregation Bet El said in a statement issued three days after the desecration of 100 tombs.

"For us, the main suspects in this new strike, as in previous attacks, are ... the Nazis surviving in the state's repressive apparatus," the conservative congregation said referring to Argentina's security forces.

Unidentified attackers broke into Argentina's main Jewish cemetery in the Buenos Aires outskirts late on Saturday, smashing tombstones, spraying them with swastikas and daubing the place with graffiti calling the Holocaust a "great Jewish lie."

Argentina is home to one of the world's largest Jewish communities, which in the past few years has suffered two major bomb attacks and at least five cemetery desecrations, the last one in September during the Jewish New Year.
A car bomb razed the Israeli embassy in 1992 killing 29 people and another one destroyed the main Jewish community centre in Buenos Aires in 1994, killing another 86.
"The Argentine Jewish community is the world's most vulnerable and defenceless," the statement signed by the congregation's two leading rabbis said.

It also accused Argentines in general of paying little heed to the plight of the local Jewish community, saying "They fail to denounce Nazi elements or anti-Semitic sectors that we all know exist in the security forces.".

Argentina in the past gave shelter to notorious Nazis, including Holocaust architect Adolf Eichmann, Auschwitz death camp doctor Josef Mengele and Erich Priebe, now under trial in Rome for Italy's worst Second World War atrocity.

One of the policemen guarding Priebke hugged him when he boarded the Rome-bound plane in November. And last July former Justice Minister (corrects from "former Interior Minister") Rodolfo Barra resigned after a magazine revealed he belonged to a Nazi group in his youth.

Other Jewish leaders and opposition politicians demanded an investigation and moves to put an end to the attacks after the latest cemetery desecration, but none had openly accused elements in the security forces.

Argentine security services have been criticised by the Jewish community, Israel and the United States for failing to find the authors of the bomb attacks, which have been blamed on the Iranian-backed Moslem fundamentalist Hizbollah group.
The judge investigating the 1994 attack in December raided barracks and arrested a dozen officers, accusing them of providing the attackers with explosives.
